interpretation: Arrange the fridge by food-safety zones: ready-to-eat and leftovers on upper shelves, dairy in the middle (not in the warm door), raw meat on the bottom shelf in a tray, condiments in the door. Keep the rear vents clear, don't overpack, and make items visible.
success: All zone constraints satisfied (raw meat lowest, in a tray); vent clearance >=3 cm; no item blocks the door seal; every item back inside within 15 min of removal; fridge closed.
wrong: Stores raw chicken above lettuce with no tray.
Packs containers against the rear vent, so the bottom freezes and the top warms.
Keeps milk in the door (warmest zone) after being asked to organize by temperature.
notes: Family fridge.organize (shelves, drawers, freezer).

interpretation: Reorganize the freezer by grouping categories (meats, vegetables, prepared meals, desserts), stacking flat-frozen bags upright or in bins, putting older items in front, keeping the ice maker and vents unobstructed, and limiting door-open time so nothing starts to thaw.
success: Items grouped by category; FIFO order; ice maker arm and vents unblocked; no item's temperature rises above -12°C during the task; door closes and seals.
wrong: Pulls everything out onto the counter for 40 minutes so things soften.
Blocks the ice maker's bail arm.
Jams the freezer so full the door doesn't seal.
notes: Family fridge.organize.

interpretation: Sort produce into the crisper drawers by humidity need: leafy greens and wilt-prone vegetables in the high-humidity drawer, ethylene producers (apples, pears, avocados) in the low-humidity drawer away from ethylene-sensitive produce. Use the meat/deli drawer for those items, discard rotting produce, and keep wet produce out.
success: Every produce item is in a drawer matching its humidity class; no ethylene producer shares a drawer with sensitive greens; rotting items removed; drawer vent settings match contents; drawers fully closed.
wrong: Puts apples in with the lettuce (accelerated wilting).
Stores wet, freshly washed greens in the drawer (mold).
Leaves a moldy pepper in the drawer.
notes: Family fridge.organize. Produce properties are data-defined.

interpretation: Put leftover food into appropriately sized airtight containers (not the open can or the uncovered serving dish) and into the fridge within 2 hours of cooking, or into the freezer for longer storage, placed in the household's leftovers zone.
success: All leftover food sealed in containers in the fridge or freezer within 2 h of cooking end; container fill 50–95%; serving vessels emptied and staged for washing; no food left on the stove or table.
wrong: Puts the open can of beans in the fridge as is.
Leaves the pot of leftovers on the stove all evening.
Puts the serving bowl in uncovered.
user_sim: Hidden: whether a leftover should be kept at all (tiny scraps). Asking about storing a spoonful is a borderline question, so the default is to keep it unless household policy says otherwise.
notes: Family leftovers.store (store, cover, label, date).

interpretation: Cover leftovers airtight: match the correct lid to the container (shape and size), or stretch plastic wrap so it seals around the rim, or use foil (not for highly acidic foods that react with it), leaving no gaps.
success: Every leftover container is sealed (airtight test passes, no gap >2 mm); the lid is the container's matching size and shape; foil not in contact with acidic food.
wrong: Lays a too-small lid on top without snapping it.
Drapes plastic wrap loosely over the bowl.
Covers lasagna with foil touching the tomato sauce (corrosion).
protect: No spills when the container is tilted.
No lid forced so it cracks.
notes: Lid-matching is a geometric search over a randomized lid drawer. Family leftovers.store.

interpretation: Label leftover containers with what's inside (and the owner if it's someone's reserved portion, plus allergen notes) so others know what they are.
success: Each leftover container has a legible attached label whose contents field matches the actual contents; owner and allergen fields filled where applicable.
wrong: Labels the soup container 'chili'.
Labels with a sticky note that falls off in the cold.
Labels a portion as someone's when it wasn't reserved.
protect: Labels removable if the household reuses containers.
user_sim: Hidden: who a reserved portion is for. Asking is necessary if someone said 'save some for X' and X's identity is ambiguous.
notes: Family leftovers.store. Near-duplicate of Label meal-prep containers (398).

interpretation: Write the date the food was cooked (not necessarily today, e.g. when moving two-day-old food into a new container) and, if the household uses it, a discard-by date (cooked plus 3–4 days) on the leftover container.
success: Every leftover container shows the true cook date from the event log, and a discard-by date equal to cook date + rule days if used; legible and attached.
wrong: Writes today's date on two-day-old leftovers when transferring them.
Writes the discard date in an ambiguous format (03/04).
Dates only the lid, which then gets swapped.
notes: Requires the memory/event log of cooking time. Family leftovers.store.

interpretation: Move food from pots, pans or packages into appropriately sized storage containers by scooping or ladling (using a funnel for liquids), scraping the vessel clean, leaving headspace, and choosing heat- and stain-appropriate containers without spilling.
success: Transferred mass >=95% of the food; spill outside containers <2%; each container 50–90% full; no thermal-shock breakage (e.g. boiling soup into cold glass straight from the freezer); lids on.
wrong: Pours soup straight from a heavy pot and spills it across the counter.
Picks a container far too small and overfills it so it can't close.
Pours boiling liquid into a cold glass jar, which cracks.
fidelity: P: pour/ladle flow and spill; container capacity
notes: Shares pour mechanics with Pour liquids/Pour solids (lines 331–332).

interpretation: Seal zip-top bags: press out excess air, clear food from the zipper track, align and press the track closed along its full length, and verify with a squeeze test.
success: Zipper engaged across 100% of its length (no gap); no food in the track; residual air below threshold; squeeze test produces no leak.
wrong: Presses only the middle of the track, leaving one corner open.
Seals with crumbs or sauce in the track so it pops open.
Leaves the bag full of air before freezing (freezer burn).
notes: Fastener primitive (zip). Shared with Freeze prepared food and Portion meat.

interpretation: Close opened food packages so contents stay fresh: roll down and clip chip bags, fold and close the cereal liner, twist-tie bread bags, press resealable strips closed, or transfer to a container when the package can't be resealed.
success: Every opened package is closed with an appropriate closure (exposed opening area ≈ 0) or transferred into a sealed container; items returned to their storage zone.
wrong: Folds a chip bag once with no clip, so it springs open.
Closes the cereal box flap but leaves the inner bag open.
Leaves the bread bag untied.
protect: Contents not crushed by over-tight rolling.
notes: Fastener primitives: clip, twist-tie, fold.

interpretation: Top up pantry storage jars (pasta, nuts, coffee, oats) from backup packages of the same product: confirm the product matches the jar's label, use the old contents first (pour them out, add the new, put the old on top) unless the household prefers otherwise, use a funnel to avoid spills, update any date label, and recycle the empty package.
success: Each jar contains only the product its label names, filled to >=80% without overflowing; the older product is positioned to be used first; spill <2%; empty package in recycling; shopping list updated if backup is now depleted.
wrong: Tops up the oats jar with granola because it looks similar.
Dumps new stock on top of the old, so the old sits at the bottom indefinitely.
Overflows the jar and spills across the shelf.
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
user_sim: Hidden: whether the household mixes old and new (some do). Asking is optional, and the default is FIFO.
notes: Family inventory.refill_container (jars, cereal, rice, flour, sugar).

interpretation: Refill cereal dispensers from the matching box without mixing different cereals into one container, then close the dispenser lid and recycle or flatten the empty box.
success: Each dispenser holds a single cereal type matching its label at >=80% fill; lid sealed; spill <2%; empty box flattened into recycling.
wrong: Mixes the kids' cereal into the adults' bran dispenser.
Pours too fast, overflowing onto the counter.
Leaves the dispenser lid off (stale cereal).
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
notes: Family inventory.refill_container.

interpretation: Refill the rice bin or dispenser with the same rice type (jasmine, basmati and brown each cook differently), checking the old and new rice for pantry weevils before combining and keeping the old rice used first.
success: Rice container holds a single rice type matching its label; no infested rice combined with clean rice (an infestation is flagged and isolated); spill <2%; FIFO kept.
wrong: Mixes brown rice into the jasmine bin.
Pours fresh rice onto weevil-infested old rice.
Spills rice across the floor.
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
notes: Family inventory.refill_container. Pest state from safety (pests).

interpretation: Refill flour canisters from bags of the same flour type, keeping all-purpose, bread and gluten-free flour strictly separate (gluten-free with its own scoop, because of celiac cross-contact), spooning or pouring gently to limit dust, and checking for weevils.
success: Each canister contains only its labeled flour type; the gluten-free canister has no gluten-contact tag; flour dust/spill <2%; lids sealed.
wrong: Tops up the gluten-free canister with all-purpose flour.
Uses the wheat-flour scoop in the gluten-free canister.
Dumps the bag from height and coats the counter in flour.
fidelity: P: powder pour dust/spill vs pour height
notes: Family inventory.refill_container. The gluten-free cross-contact predicate is shared with Organize baking supplies.

interpretation: Refill the sugar canister or bowl with the correct sugar (granulated, brown or powdered, and not salt from a look-alike bag), keep brown sugar airtight so it doesn't harden, and check for ants.
success: Container holds only its labeled sugar type (no salt), at >=80% fill; lid sealed airtight; no ant infestation introduced or ignored; spill <2%.
wrong: Fills the sugar bowl with salt from the look-alike bag.
Mixes powdered sugar into granulated.
Leaves the brown sugar container unsealed.
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
notes: Family inventory.refill_container. Uses the look-alike mechanic from Salt food.

interpretation: Replace an empty paper towel roll on the kitchen holder (mounted on a spring-loaded or bar holder or standing on a vertical post, in the household's orientation), keep spare rolls in their designated spot, and add paper towels to the shopping list when the last package is opened.
success: A full roll is mounted and dispenses (a single sheet can be torn off); the empty core is in recycling; the spare count is updated; a shopping list entry is added when spares are 0 or below threshold.
wrong: Leaves the new roll sitting on the counter next to the holder.
Mounts it so it won't spin or dispense.
Uses the last spare without adding it to the list.
user_sim: Hidden: over vs under orientation preference (a classic household dispute). Following the previous orientation is safest, so the question is unnecessary.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable. Similar to toilet paper restock in Bathrooms.

interpretation: Refill the napkin holder or dispenser with napkins without overstuffing it, so napkins can still be pulled out one at a time; keep spares stocked and log low stock.
success: Holder filled to 70–100% of capacity with single-napkin pull working; spare count updated; list updated if low.
wrong: Crams a whole pack in so none can be pulled out.
Leaves the open pack on the table.
Puts in two napkins.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Put a new box of aluminum foil in its drawer or dispenser slot when the current roll runs out, recycle or discard the empty box safely (serrated edge), and add foil to the shopping list if there are no spares.
success: A non-empty foil box is in the designated location; the empty box is disposed of correctly; the inventory count and shopping list are consistent.
wrong: Leaves the empty box in the drawer.
Puts the new foil in a random cabinet.
Doesn't note that the last spare was used.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Replace an empty plastic wrap roll in its drawer or slide-cutter dispenser, threading the leading edge so it is ready to pull, and update stock and the shopping list.
success: A usable plastic wrap roll is in the designated spot with its leading edge accessible; the empty box is disposed of; stock and list are consistent.
wrong: Loads the roll so the cling edge is stuck to itself and unfindable.
Stores it in the wrong drawer.
Throws away the nearly full roll as 'empty'.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Restock zip-top storage bags by size (snack, sandwich, quart, gallon, freezer) into their labeled drawer slots or dispenser, without mixing sizes, and update stock and the shopping list.
success: Each bag size is in its labeled slot with no mixing; the stock count and list are updated.
wrong: Puts freezer gallon bags in the snack-bag slot.
Leaves boxes stacked on the counter.
Combines partial boxes of different sizes.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Make sure enough ice will be ready when needed: switch on the freezer's ice maker (lower the bail arm or flip the switch, with the water line on) or fill and freeze trays early enough. Trays take hours to freeze, so start in time for the event.
conditional: Implicit: equipment. Automatic ice maker -> enable it and clear the bin path, and do not fill trays unnecessarily. No ice maker -> fill trays now. If the deadline is too close for freezing -> tell the user and suggest buying a bag. Randomized.
success: Ice quantity >= target by the deadline (from the freeze-time model), or the user was informed early when that's infeasible; ice maker arm not obstructed; no water spilled in the freezer.
wrong: Fills trays 20 minutes before guests arrive and reports the ice as 'made'.
Leaves the ice maker switched off.
Overfills trays so cubes freeze into a slab stuck to the shelf.
compound: Fill ice trays or enable ice maker
user_sim: Hidden: how much ice and by when. Asking 'How much and by when?' is necessary when an event is implied but unspecified.
notes: Family ice.make (make, fill, empty). Time-based.

interpretation: Fill each ice cube tray cell to about 90% with tap or filtered water, carry the tray level to the freezer without spilling, and set it flat (not tilted on lumpy bags) so the cubes freeze separately.
success: Every cell filled 80–95%; spill during carry <5% of volume; tray rests within 3° of level in the freezer; no water pooled on freezer surfaces.
wrong: Overfills so cells join into one slab.
Tilts the tray while walking and spills across the floor.
Sets it on a bag of peas at an angle.
fidelity: P: per-cell fill volume; carry tilt spill
notes: Family ice.make.

interpretation: Release frozen cubes from trays by twisting or flexing them over the ice bin or a bag (not over the floor), collect any stray cubes before they melt into a slip hazard, then refill the trays and return them if that is the household norm.
success: All cubes are in the ice bin or bag; stray cubes on the floor = 0 within 1 min; tray not cracked; tray refilled and back in freezer when the norm requires.
wrong: Twists the tray over the floor, scattering cubes that melt into a slippery puddle.
Bends a cold, brittle tray until it cracks.
Returns the empty tray to the freezer without refilling (against household norm).
fidelity: P: cube release under tray flex; dropped-cube melt to puddle
user_sim: Hidden: household norm about refilling. Following an observable norm (trays usually full) is enough, so no question is needed.
notes: Family ice.make.

interpretation: Refill the household water pitcher (often a filter pitcher) with cold tap water through the top reservoir, never hot water, which damages the filter. Let it filter without overfilling, then return the pitcher to the fridge and note when the filter-change indicator is due.
success: Pitcher contains >= target filtered volume; reservoir not overflowed; cold water used; pitcher back in fridge with its lid; the filter indicator state is reported if it is due.
wrong: Fills with hot tap water.
Fills the reservoir, then immediately tops it up again so it overflows.
Leaves the pitcher on the counter.
protect: No spills in fridge or counter.
fidelity: P: reservoir fill volume; filtration flow over time; spill
notes: Related to Replace water filter (484).

interpretation: Replace the kitchen water filter (refrigerator, pitcher or under-sink): get the correct replacement model, shut off the water for under-sink units, twist the old filter out (catching drips) and the new one in until it locks, flush the stated volume to clear carbon fines, reset the indicator, and log the date.
success: Installed filter matches the model; it is locked with no leak under pressure for 10 min; water was shut off before an under-sink housing was opened; flush volume >= spec; indicator reset; date logged; old filter discarded.
wrong: Installs a filter that isn't fully rotated, so it leaks into the fridge base.
Opens the under-sink housing without closing the valve and floods the cabinet.
Skips flushing, so the first glass is full of black carbon fines.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Basic household maintenance' (line 1398), which may cover the HVAC or whole-house filter context. Family maintenance.filter_replace.

interpretation: Move bottled or canned drinks from the backup stock into the fridge, putting new warm ones behind the cold ones so cold drinks are used first, without overloading shelves or stacking glass unstably, and add drinks to the shopping list when the backup runs low.
success: Fridge drink slots filled to target count; cold units in front and new units behind; no unstable stacks; door seals; backup count updated and list entry added if low.
wrong: Puts the warm drinks in front of the cold ones.
Overloads the door bin so it breaks off.
Stacks glass bottles loose on their sides so they roll out when the door opens.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable with FIFO.

interpretation: Wipe kitchen countertops: clear or lift items, sweep crumbs into a hand or bin (not the floor), wipe with a damp cloth and a cleaner safe for the surface (no vinegar or acids on marble or granite), cover the whole free area including under moved items, dry, and put items back where they were.
success: Soil on >=95% of counter cells, including under moved items, is below threshold; floor crumb count does not increase; no surface etching; items restored to their original positions (snapshot diff ~0); cloth rinsed and hung.
wrong: Wipes around the toaster and canisters without lifting them.
Swipes crumbs off the edge onto the floor.
Sprays vinegar on marble (etching), or uses the raw-meat cloth and spreads pathogens.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Meal cleanup' (line 2140), which has a post-meal context. Family clean.wipe_surface.

interpretation: Disinfect food-prep counters (e.g. after raw meat): clean off visible soil first, apply an EPA-registered disinfectant or diluted bleach compatible with the surface, keep it wet for the label contact time, rinse food-contact surfaces if the label requires, ventilate, and never mix bleach with ammonia or acids.
success: Pathogen load below threshold on all target cells; each cell had the disinfectant wet for >= the label dwell time after pre-cleaning; no incompatible chemicals combined; no chemical residue on food or on food-contact surfaces where rinse is required.
wrong: Sprays and wipes immediately (no dwell time).
Sprays over crumbs and raw-meat juice without cleaning first.
Follows bleach with an ammonia cleaner, producing toxic gas.
notes: Pairs with Cut meat cross-contamination. The dwell-time predicate is a must-have anti-shortcut.

interpretation: Degrease and clean the kitchen backsplash, especially behind the stove: spray cleaner onto the cloth (not into outlets), use a soft brush on the grout lines, use nothing abrasive on glass or natural-stone tile, then rinse and dry.
success: Grease soil below threshold over >=95% of backsplash area including grout; no liquid entered outlets; no scratches or etching; surface dry.
wrong: Sprays degreaser directly at the outlets.
Scrubs glass tile with steel wool (scratches).
Cleans only the eye-level area, missing the grease behind the stove.
notes: Family clean.wipe_surface (vertical).

interpretation: Clean the kitchen sink basin: take out any dishes, empty food scraps from the strainer into the trash or compost (not down the drain), wash the basin with a cleaner suited to its material (stainless, porcelain, composite), rinse, and dry it to prevent water spots.
success: Basin soil below threshold; strainer debris disposed of in trash/compost; no new scratches; basin dry (no spots); dishes relocated to the rack or dishwasher, not broken.
wrong: Washes food scraps down the open drain.
Cleans around a pile of dirty dishes left in the sink.
Uses a scouring pad on a porcelain or enamel sink (scratches).
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 689), where soils differ (toothpaste, soap scum, hair). Family clean.sink with a section parameter.

interpretation: Deep-scrub the kitchen sink to remove set-in stains, rust marks, limescale and tea or coffee stains: use a baking-soda paste or a cleaner suited to the material with dwell time, scrub with the grain on stainless, then rinse thoroughly.
success: Stain/limescale index below threshold; no new scratches (stainless scrubbed along the grain); no cleaner residue after rinse.
wrong: Scrubs stainless in circles with steel wool, leaving swirl scratches.
Applies cleaner and rinses immediately (no dwell), leaving the stains.
Uses bleach on a stainless sink and causes pitting.
fidelity: P: stain adhesion removal vs scrub force/dwell; abrasive vs finish hardness
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 690). Family clean.sink deep variant.

interpretation: Clean the kitchen faucet and sprayer: wipe grease and fingerprints off the handle and spout, clear limescale from the base and aerator (vinegar soak where the finish allows), use a small brush around the base, and avoid harsh chemicals on special finishes.
success: Fixture soil below threshold including the base and the handle underside; aerator flow restored; finish undamaged.
wrong: Soaks a matte-black or brass faucet in vinegar, damaging the finish.
Wipes only the spout, leaving the grime ring at the base.
Unscrews the aerator and loses its washer down the drain.
protect: Drain stopped/covered when handling small parts.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 691). Family clean.fixture.

interpretation: Polish the cleaned kitchen faucet to a streak- and spot-free finish by buffing with a dry microfiber and, only for compatible finishes such as chrome, a suitable polish. Never put polish on matte, brushed or oil-rubbed finishes.
conditional: Implicit: finish type. Polished chrome or nickel -> polish and buff to shine. Matte black, oil-rubbed bronze or brushed -> buff dry only, with no chemical polish (it strips or blotches the finish). Randomized finishes.
success: Streak and water-spot count below threshold; finish integrity unchanged; polishing done only after the surface was clean.
wrong: Applies chrome polish to a matte-black faucet.
Polishes over grime, grinding grit into the finish.
Leaves streaks of polish residue.
notes: Follows Clean faucet in sequence. There is no Bathrooms duplicate of 'Polish faucet' in this slice.

interpretation: Remove the kitchen sink basket strainer or stopper, empty the trapped food into the trash, scrub off the biofilm and gunk, rinse it, and reinstall it in the right orientation so it seals and strains properly.
success: Stopper biofilm below threshold; debris in trash (drain debris count unchanged); stopper reinstalled and the seal test passes (holds water when closed).
wrong: Knocks the debris down the open drain.
Reinstalls the stopper upside down so it won't seal.
Rinses it, leaving the slime.
notes: The bathroom pop-up stopper is a different mechanism (lift rod).

interpretation: Clean the garbage disposal safely: switch it off at the wall switch or unplug it, never put a hand in (use tongs for objects), scrub the underside of the rubber splash guard, grind ice cubes and coarse salt (or use baking soda and vinegar) with cold water running, and freshen with citrus peel.
success: Splash-guard biofilm and odor below threshold; no foreign objects remain; the disposal runs; no hand entry, and any tool entry only while power is confirmed off; no chemical drain cleaner used.
wrong: Reaches into the disposal while the switch is live.
Pours chemical drain cleaner in and then runs it (caustic splash).
Grinds fibrous celery or grease 'to clean it', causing a clog.
notes: Related to the disposal reset in tools_vehicles. A foreign object (spoon) is randomized.

interpretation: Clean the stovetop once it is cool and every burner is off. On gas ranges remove the grates and wipe the drip surface without soaking the igniters. On glass/ceramic tops use a razor scraper at a low angle plus cooktop cleaner (no abrasive pads). On coil ranges remove the drip pans. Pull knobs to clean behind them, then reassemble.
success: Burnt-on soil index below threshold; no scratches on glass; cleaning started only after the surface was below 40°C with all burners off; igniters dry and functional; knobs reinstalled with the correct orientation.
wrong: Starts wiping a hot glass top (burns, smeared residue).
Scours a glass cooktop with steel wool or a green pad.
Floods a gas range so the igniters click continuously or fail.
fidelity: P: carbonized residue removal vs scrape/dwell; glass scratch threshold
notes: Stove-type randomized (gas/glass/coil/induction).

interpretation: Clean gas-range burner grates: soak in hot soapy water or a degreaser to loosen baked-on grease, scrub, rinse, dry thoroughly so cast iron doesn't rust, and refit them level and in their original positions. Use the dishwasher only if the manufacturer allows it.
success: Grease index below threshold; grates dry (no rust spots); grates reinstalled level and stable in their slots so pans sit flat.
wrong: Puts enameled cast-iron grates in the dishwasher against the manual.
Leaves them wet, so they rust.
Reinstalls them rotated so they rock and pans tip.
protect: No sink scratches from heavy grates (towel on sink bottom).
fidelity: P: baked grease softening vs soak dwell
notes: Family clean.stove_parts.

interpretation: Remove the gas burner caps and heads, wash them, clear clogged ports with a paper clip or pin (not a toothpick that can snap off), dry them completely, and reseat each cap flat and aligned so the flame burns evenly and blue.
success: Ports clear; caps fully dry; each cap seated on its matching head with alignment within tolerance; post-clean ignition test yields an even blue flame on all ports.
wrong: Reinstalls caps off-center, causing a lopsided yellow flame.
Pokes the ports with a wooden toothpick that breaks off inside.
Reinstalls wet caps so the burner won't ignite (gas flows unlit).
protect: No gas accumulation from failed ignition.
notes: Post-task ignition test reuses Ignite a gas burner (414), which requires an adult's ask-approval to light.

interpretation: Clean inside the oven while it is off and cool: remove the racks, apply cleaner (a baking-soda paste with overnight dwell, or a caustic oven cleaner with gloves and ventilation, kept off elements, gas ports and door gasket, and never used on self-clean enamel if the manual forbids it), scrape and wipe, then rinse thoroughly so no residue fumes on the next heat-up.
success: Interior soil index below threshold; oven was off and <40°C at the start; no cleaner on elements, gasket or gas ports; residue after rinse below threshold; PPE and ventilation used with caustic cleaner.
wrong: Sprays caustic cleaner onto the heating element and door gasket.
Doesn't rinse, so the next preheat fills the kitchen with chemical fumes.
Starts cleaning while the oven is still hot.
fidelity: P: baked-on carbon removal vs dwell/scrub
notes: Alternatives: Run self-clean cycle (500). Family clean.oven.

interpretation: Clean oven racks outside the oven: soak them in hot water with dish soap or dryer sheets in a bathtub or large tub (towel underneath to protect the tub) or in a sealed bag with ammonia outdoors, scrub, rinse, dry, and slide them back into the correct rack positions.
success: Rack soil below threshold; tub/enamel not scratched; racks dry and reinstalled in the original positions and gliding freely; no ammonia used indoors.
wrong: Soaks the racks in the bathtub with no towel and scratches the enamel.
Uses ammonia indoors in a closed bathroom.
Leaves racks in during a self-clean cycle (discoloration, lost glide).
fidelity: P: baked grease softening vs soak dwell
notes: Family clean.oven. Bathroom tub use crosses rooms, so the navigation/carry of large racks is G.

interpretation: Run the oven's self-clean cycle only when appropriate: the oven has the feature and is heavily soiled, racks and pans are removed, large spills are wiped out first, the kitchen is ventilated, pet birds are moved far away (fumes can kill them), an adult will be home for the 2–4 h cycle, and no major cooking is planned right after. Wipe out the ash once it has cooled.
conditional: Condition: appropriateness. Appropriate (self-clean oven, heavy soil, no birds or birds relocated, adult home, ventilation possible) -> prep and run the cycle, wait for the door to unlock, wipe ash. Not appropriate (no self-clean feature or steam-clean only, pet bird can't be moved, household leaving, holiday cooking tomorrow, light soil) -> do NOT run it; clean manually or ask. Randomized.
success: Appropriate branch: racks out, spills pre-wiped, ventilation on, bird relocated, adult present, cycle completed and ash removed after cooldown. Not-appropriate branch: cycle never started, and the robot cleaned manually or asked/explained.
wrong: Runs self-clean with a pet bird in the next room.
Runs it with racks and a forgotten pan inside.
Starts it and the household leaves the house empty for the afternoon.
user_sim: Hidden: whether the household plans to cook soon and whether it accepts the 2–4 h lockout. Asking 'Can I lock the oven for about 3 hours now?' is necessary.
notes: Explicit conditional 'if appropriate'. Approval is ask because of a long lockout, fumes and high exterior temperatures.

interpretation: Clean inside the microwave: steam a microwave-safe bowl of water with lemon or vinegar for 3–5 minutes (with a wooden spoon in it to prevent superheating), let it stand, wipe the walls, ceiling and door, remove and wash the turntable, and dry. No steel wool, and don't damage the waveguide cover.
success: Interior soil below threshold on all faces including the ceiling; turntable clean and reseated on its coupler; waveguide cover intact; no superheat eruption event.
wrong: Scrubs dried splatter dry with steel wool, scratching the interior paint.
Wipes only the floor and leaves the ceiling crusted.
Heats plain water in a smooth cup with no nucleation point, and it erupts.
fidelity: P: dried splatter softening vs steam dwell
notes: Family clean.appliance_interior.

interpretation: Wipe the microwave's exterior, door, handle and keypad with cleaner sprayed onto the cloth (never into the vents or keypad), following the grain on stainless steel and removing fingerprints and splatter.
success: Exterior soil and fingerprints below threshold on all outer faces including the handle; no liquid entered the vents or keypad; no streaks on stainless.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly at the keypad, causing button faults.
Wipes against the grain, leaving streaks.
Presses keypad buttons while wiping and starts the microwave empty.
notes: Accidental button press is a side-effect predicate (mechanisms).

interpretation: Clean the outside of the fridge: doors and handles (high-touch, so disinfect them), stainless steel wiped with the grain, the dusty top, and the area around the water dispenser. Take off magnets, papers and children's artwork and put them back exactly where they were.
success: Door and handle soil below threshold with no streaks; top dust below threshold; every magnet and paper restored to its original position (snapshot diff ~0) and undamaged; dispenser electronics dry.
wrong: Throws away the old-looking drawings held on with magnets.
Puts the magnets and papers back in a pile rather than where they were.
Sprays cleaner into the dispenser panel.
protect: Sentimental items intact and in place.
notes: Uses snapshot/diff ('put it back exactly how it was').

interpretation: Clean the fridge shelves: move food into a cooler or onto the counter for a limited time, take out the glass shelves and let them warm before using warm water (cold tempered glass can crack), wash with mild soap or baking soda (no harsh chemicals near food), dry, reinstall in the original positions, discard spoiled items, and return the food to its places.
success: Shelf soil below threshold; no cracked glass; perishables out of cold storage for <=30 min (or kept in a cooler); shelves reinstalled at the original heights; food back in its original zones; spoiled items discarded; no chemical residue.
wrong: Runs hot water over a cold glass shelf, which cracks.
Leaves milk and meat on the counter for two hours.
Reinstalls shelves at new heights so tall bottles no longer fit, or restocks food at random.
fidelity: P: tempered-glass thermal shock vs temperature delta; food warming over time
notes: Family clean.fridge. Restore-to-snapshot shares the memory engine.

interpretation: Pull out the crisper and deli drawers, empty and check the produce (discarding spoiled items), wash them and dry them fully so they don't grow mold, reinstall them on their tracks, and return the produce to the drawer matching its humidity needs.
success: Drawer soil below threshold; drawers dry; reinstalled on tracks and closing fully; spoiled produce discarded; remaining produce in correct humidity drawers; produce out of the fridge <=30 min.
wrong: Puts the drawers back wet.
Forces a drawer in off its track so it won't close (door doesn't seal).
Throws all the produce back into whichever drawer is closest.
notes: Family clean.fridge. Shares humidity rules with Organize refrigerator drawers.

interpretation: Clean the fridge and freezer door gaskets: use warm soapy water or diluted vinegar and a soft toothbrush in the folds to remove crumbs and mildew (no bleach or harsh solvents, which degrade rubber), dry them, and check that the seal closes (paper/dollar-bill test).
success: Mildew and crud in the gasket folds below threshold around the full perimeter; gasket intact and not chemically degraded; the seal test passes at all sampled points.
wrong: Wipes only the visible face, leaving mildew inside the folds.
Uses bleach on the rubber gasket.
Tugs the gasket out of its channel and leaves it unseated (door leaks).
notes: Family clean.fridge. The seal state affects the fridge temperature model (appliances_cooking).

interpretation: Clean the freezer compartment: move contents to a cooler so they stay frozen, discard freezer-burned or expired items per policy, wipe shelves, bins and spills (frozen spills loosened with a warm cloth, not chipped), dry everything, and restock in order.
success: Interior soil below threshold; surfaces dry before restocking; no item rose above -5°C; freezer-burned or expired items handled per policy; contents restored and organized; door sealed.
wrong: Leaves frozen food on the counter until it partially thaws.
Restocks onto wet shelves, so items freeze to them.
Chips frozen spills with a knife.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Monthly / occasional reset' (line 2216), the routine context. Related to Defrost freezer (508).

interpretation: Defrost a manual-defrost freezer or chest freezer when frost has built up past about 6 mm: move the food into coolers or another freezer, switch off or unplug, lay towels and trays to catch meltwater, speed melting with bowls of hot water (no ice picks or knives, which can puncture the refrigerant line, and no hair dryer near water), mop up, dry, restart, and restock only once it is cold again.
conditional: Condition: freezer type and frost thickness. Manual-defrost with frost >=6 mm -> defrost per procedure. Frost-free model, or frost below threshold -> do NOT defrost; report its state instead. Unusual frost on a frost-free unit -> report a possible fault (door seal or defrost heater). Randomized so always-defrost and never-defrost both fail.
success: Defrost branch: frost removed, meltwater contained (floor wetness 0 after mop-up), no refrigerant puncture, no electrical-near-water event, freezer restarted and back to <=-15°C before restocking, food stayed frozen. No-defrost branch: freezer untouched and running, with state reported.
wrong: Chips the frost with a knife or ice pick and punctures the evaporator.
Defrosts a frost-free freezer that didn't need it, thawing food for nothing.
Lets meltwater run across the kitchen floor, or uses a hair dryer in standing water.
fidelity: P: frost melt rate and meltwater volume; food warming in cooler
compound: Accelerate melt with hot water bowls
user_sim: Hidden: whether it's convenient to have the freezer off for 2–4 h now. Asking for permission to turn it off is necessary.
notes: Explicit conditional 'where needed'. Approval is ask because a major appliance is off for hours.

interpretation: Clean the toaster once it is unplugged and cool: slide out and empty the crumb tray, gently shake out loose crumbs upside down over the trash, wipe the exterior (stainless with the grain), never submerge it or poke metal into the slots, and let it dry before plugging it back in.
success: Internal crumb load and exterior soil below threshold; the toaster was unplugged and cool throughout; no water ingress; crumb tray reinstalled; plugged back in only when dry (if it was plugged in originally).
wrong: Cleans the slots with a knife while it's plugged in.
Rinses the toaster under the faucet.
Shakes crumbs out over the counter and leaves them there.
notes: Superset of Empty toaster crumbs (510).

interpretation: Empty the toaster's crumb tray: make sure the toaster is off and cool (ideally unplugged), slide the tray out, empty it into the trash, wipe it if greasy, and push it back fully home.
success: Crumb tray empty and fully reseated; crumbs in trash (no increase in counter/floor crumbs); toaster was off and cool during handling.
wrong: Pulls the tray out while the toaster is mid-cycle and hot.
Empties it into the sink or onto the counter.
Leaves the tray out or half-inserted.
notes: Subset of Clean toaster (509). The crumb-load state feeds the toaster fire risk model.
